To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
six mutations in the TNSALPs gene were identified in three unrelated Chinese children with hypophosphatasias.

six missense mutations in the TNSALp gene were identified in three independent pedigrees with hypophosphatasias, and the mutations resulted in decreased expression and/or enzymatic activity of TNSALp protein, and thus caused the disease.
the low activity in three Chinese children with hypophosphatasias is mainly due to a defect in protein expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the pathogenesis of hypophosphatasias and may provide a molecular basis for future genetic counseling and treatment of this disease.
the genetic analysis of hypophosphatasias in Chinese children.
the identification of mutations in the TNSALPs gene and the characterization of the molecular mechanism of hypophosphatasias.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the six missense mutants in the TNSALPs are associated with the clinical features of hypophosphatasias.
hypophosphatasias is a genetically and clinically heterogeneous disease.
the six mutations identified in our study are responsible for the hypophosphatasias in our patients, and these mutations are likely to be the major cause for the disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mutations identified in the three pedigrees are associated with a dominant-negative effect, which is the main cause of the disease in these families.
the six missense mutants are associated with hypophosphatasic phenotypes.
the low activity in these patients may be due to the decreased protein expression in both immature forms (66 KD) and mature forms (80 KD) of the mutant proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TNSALp protein is essential for the normal mineralization of bone.
the low activity in the serum ALP is due to a defect in TNSALP expression, not to a defect in enzymatic activity.
we have identified the mutations in three Chinese patients and have characterized the molecular defects of these mutations.
